One claim changed. TensorRT-LLM v1.4.0rc0 (2026-10-14T16:35:44Z, release candidate) supersedes the v1.3.0rc29 recorded by the previous pass, and the supersession is one the previous pass left open: the 2026-10-15 pass re-read vLLM and SGLang and recorded them as holding, but did not re-state a TensorRT-LLM version of its own, so the newer release candidate stood recorded only in the older paragraph that still describes v1.3.0rc29 as having no successor. v1.4.0rc0 removes the Python backend of KVCacheManagerV2 and migrates LlmRequest fields to Python, both breaking, so the solution description and limitations are rewritten around those two changes rather than around the AutoDeploy and cpp_only removals that belonged to v1.3.0rc29. On model support it adds GLM-5.3-Flash, K-EXAONE-2, Qwen-Image-Layered, static FP8 Cosmos3 Nano and Super checkpoints, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL, NVFP4 KV cache support for MiniMax-M3 and the MiniMax H3 ref2va mode; on the API side it adds command-line configuration overrides, per-request speculative-decoding acceptance reporting, OpenAI-style errors when a request exceeds the context length, a per-model serving-extension registry and OpenEngine gRPC bindings shipped in the wheel. It also adds a Mooncake store pool with V2 scheduler preemption, sparse KV cache configuration with tier-aware locking and offload, and VisualGen sparse attention on PrimTS. Its known issues are recorded rather than omitted, because a release candidate that lists them is not a release to plan against: multi-GPU streaming or RPC executor workloads may hang during worker initialization when MPI worker pools are reused on H100; DeepSeek MLA models may crash with an illegal memory access when CUDA graphs are captured with BF16 BMM on SM120 and SM121 GPUs; GPT-OSS models may fail with attention data parallelism on SM120 when automatic communication selects NCCL EP for unsupported hidden sizes; Qwen3 models with tied embeddings may fail at model construction when attention data parallelism is enabled with TP greater than 1; and OpenTelemetry tracing may export additional FastAPI spans when FastAPI 0.142 or newer is installed. No stable release followed it, so the record remains a release candidate and not a stable release, and the TensorRT-LLM evidence pin moves from the v1.3.0rc29 tag to the v1.4.0rc0 tag with a checkedAt of 2026-10-17.
